parts.latex:
A delivery truck was valued at \$65 000 when new. The value of the truck depreciates at a rate of 22 cents per kilometre travelled.

What is the value of the truck after it has travelled a total distance of 132 600 km?

solutions.latex:
The truck loses $22$ cents, that is $\$0.22$, for each kilometre travelled.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Depreciation} &= 132\,600 \times 0.22 \\ &= \$29\,172 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Value} &= 65\,000 - 29\,172 \\ &= \$35\,828 \end{aligned}$$
This is option A.

parts.latex:
A plumber leases equipment which is valued at \$60 000.

The salvage value of the equipment at any time can be calculated using either of the two methods of depreciation shown in the table.

\extable{300_q28_t1}

Under which method of depreciation would the salvage value of the equipment be lower at the end of 3 years? Justify your answer with appropriate mathematical calculations.

solutions.latex:
Straight-line method, using $S = V_0 - D_n$:
$$\begin{aligned}S &= 60\,000-3500\times 3\\ &= \$49\,500\end{aligned}$$
Declining-balance method, using $S = V_0(1-r)^n$:
$$\begin{aligned}S &= 60\,000(1-0.12)^3\\ &= 60\,000(0.88)^3\\ &= \$40\,888.32\end{aligned}$$
Since $\$40\,888.32 < \$49\,500$:
$$\therefore\ \text{the declining-balance method gives the lower salvage value.}$$
criteria: Correctly calculates the salvage value using the declining-balance method, or equivalent merit
Attempts to calculate the salvage value using the declining-balance method, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Straight-line formula S = V0 - D_n with D_n = 3500 per year taken from the table as in the source.

4426.stem: A company purchases a machine for \$50 000. The two methods of depreciation being considered are the declining-balance method and the straight-line method.

parts.latex:
For the declining-balance method, the salvage value of the machine after $n$ years is given by the formula

$$S = V_0 \times (0.80)^n,$$

where $S$ is the salvage value and $V_0$ is the initial value of the asset.
What is the annual rate of depreciation used in this formula?
Calculate the salvage value of the machine after 3 years, based on the given formula.

For the straight-line method, the value of the machine is depreciated at a rate of $12.2\%$ of the purchase price each year.

When will the value of the machine, using this method, be equal to the salvage value found in part (a) (ii)?

solutions.latex:
The formula is $S = V_0 \times (0.80)^n$, so each year the value is $80\%$ of the previous value.

The annual rate of depreciation is $100\% - 80\% = 20\%$.

Using the given formula with $V_0 = 50\,000$ and $n = 3$:
$$\begin{aligned} S &= 50\,000 \times (0.8)^3 \\ &= \$25\,600 \end{aligned}$$

Straight-line depreciation each year is $12.2\%$ of the purchase price.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Annual depreciation} &= 12.2\% \times 50\,000 \\ &= \$6100 \end{aligned}$$
The value after $n$ years equals the salvage value from part (a)(ii).
$$\begin{aligned} 25\,600 &= 50\,000 - 6100n \\ -24\,400 &= -6100n \\ n &= \dfrac{-24\,400}{-6100} \\ &= 4 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ n = 4 \text{ years}$$
criteria: Finds the annual depreciated amount, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
An asset is depreciated using the declining-balance method with a rate of depreciation of $8\%$ per half year. The asset was bought for \$10 000.

What is the salvage value of the asset after 5 years?

solutions.latex:
The depreciation rate is per half year, so the number of periods in 5 years is $n = 5\times 2 = 10$.

Using the declining-balance formula $S = V_0(1-r)^n$ with $V_0 = 10\,000$ and $r = 0.08$:
$$\begin{aligned} S &= 10\,000\,(1 - 0.08)^{10} \\ &= 10\,000\,(0.92)^{10} \\ &\approx \$4343.88 \end{aligned}$$
This is option C.

4520.stem:
The value, $V$, of the machine after $n$ years is given by the formula

$$V = 60000 \times 0.85^{n}$$

parts.latex: By what percentage rate will the machine depreciate annually?
Calculate the value of the machine after three years.
At the end of which year will the machine’s value first fall below $\$12\,000$?

solutions.latex:
The formula $V = 60000\times 0.85^n$ has $1 - 0.15 = 0.85$ as its multiplier.
$$\text{Depreciation rate} = 15\%$$

Substitute $n=3$.
$$\begin{aligned} V &= 60000\times 0.85^3 \\ &= \$36\,847.50 \end{aligned}$$

Test values of $n$ in $V = 60000\times 0.85^n$.
$$\begin{aligned} n=8:\ V &= 60000\times 0.85^8 = \$16\,349.43 \\ n=10:\ V &= 60000\times 0.85^{10} = \$11\,812.46 \end{aligned}$$
The value is below $\$12\,000$ at $n=10$.
$$\therefore\ \text{the value first falls below } \$12\,000 \text{ at the end of year } 10$$
criteria: Substitutes values of $n$ to show the value crossing $\$12\,000$, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source only tests n=8 and n=10; n=9 gives about $13\,897$, not shown in source, so 'first' year relies on that. Not added.

parts.latex:
Office furniture depreciates by the declining balance method at a rate of $13\dfrac{1}{3}\%$ per annum.

What is the value of office furniture that was purchased 5 years ago for \$15 000?

solutions.latex:
Declining balance: $S = V_0(1-r)^n$, with $r = 13\dfrac{1}{3}\% = \dfrac{2}{15}$, $V_0 = 15\,000$ and $n = 5$.

$$\begin{aligned} S &= 15\,000\left(1-\dfrac{2}{15}\right)^5 \\ &= 15\,000\left(\dfrac{13}{15}\right)^5 \\ &\approx \$7334 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the value is } \$7334 \text{ (option C)}$$

parts.latex:
Jaime bought a van for \$31 000 to make deliveries to customers. He applied a straight-line method of depreciation to the van.

After 3 years, the value of the van is \$19 000.

What was the annual amount of depreciation?

solutions.latex:
Let $D$ be the annual depreciation. After 3 years the value is the cost less $3D$.
$$\begin{aligned} 19\,000 &= 31\,000 - 3D \\ -12\,000 &= -3D \\ D &= \$4000 \end{aligned}$$
Alternatively, the total depreciation is $31\,000 - 19\,000 = 12\,000$, so
$$12\,000 \div 3 = \$4000$$
$$\therefore\ D = \$4000 \text{ per year}$$
criteria: Correct substitution or difference of $12\,000$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:

What is its salvage value today, to the nearest dollar?

solutions.latex:
Under declining-balance depreciation the value after $n$ years is $S = V_0(1-r)^n$, with $V_0 = 2467$, $r = 0.15$ and $n = 3$.
$$\begin{aligned} S &= 2467(1-0.15)^3\\ &= 2467(0.85)^3\\ &\approx \$1515 \end{aligned}$$
The answer is D.

6385.stem:
Tahnee bought a car for use with her small business for \$24 000.

For taxation purposes she needed to work out a depreciated value of the car each year.

She initially decided to do this using the declining balance method at a rate of 25%.

parts.latex: Show that the depreciation of the car in the first four years is more than three times greater than the depreciation between the fourth and eighth years using this method.

She decided to change to the straight-line method of depreciation, as calculations were easier, but wants the value after eight years to be same as she calculated using the declining balance method.

By what amount should she depreciate the car each year, and what percentage is this of the cars new value?

solutions.latex:
Declining balance: $V=24\,000(0.75)^n$, since the value falls 25% each year.
$$\begin{aligned} V_4 &= 24\,000(0.75)^4 = \$7593.75 \\ V_8 &= 24\,000(0.75)^8 \approx \$2402.71 \end{aligned}$$
Depreciation in the first four years:
$$\begin{aligned} 24\,000-7593.75 &= \$16\,406.25 \end{aligned}$$
Depreciation between the fourth and eighth years:
$$\begin{aligned} 7593.75-2402.71 &= \$5191.04 \end{aligned}$$
Three times the later depreciation:
$$\begin{aligned} 3\times 5191.04 &= \$15\,573.12 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ 16\,406.25>15\,573.12$$
so the depreciation in the first four years is more than three times the depreciation between the fourth and eighth years.
criteria: Finds $V_4$ and $V_8$, or the depreciation for one of the periods, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The value after eight years must be $\$2402.71$, so the total depreciation is
$$\begin{aligned} 24\,000-2402.71 &= \$21\,597.29 \end{aligned}$$
Straight-line depreciation spreads this equally over 8 years.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Yearly depreciation} &= \dfrac{21\,597.29}{8} \\ &\approx \$2699.66 \end{aligned}$$
As a percentage of the new value:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{2699.66}{24\,000}\times 100 &\approx 11.25\% \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{she should depreciate the car by about } \$2699.66 \text{ each year, which is about } 11.25\% \text{ of its new value}$$
criteria: Finds the yearly amount, or the total depreciation of $\$21\,597.29$, or equivalent merit

6551.stem:
Lauren spends \$6000 on a new photocopier for her business.

She uses the declining-balance method to calculate the depreciation of the photocopier. She claims this amount as a tax deduction each year. She can only claim the depreciation for that particular year.

parts.latex: If the rate of depreciation is $26\%$ per annum, show that the depreciation she can claim in the second year is equal to \$1154, rounded correct to the nearest dollar.

solutions.latex:
Declining-balance depreciation is $26\%$ of the value at the start of each year.

Year 1:
$$\begin{aligned} D_1 &= 0.26\times 6000 = \$1560 \\ V_1 &= 6000-1560 = \$4440 \end{aligned}$$
Year 2:
$$\begin{aligned} D_2 &= 0.26\times 4440 \\ &= \$1154.40 \\ &\approx \$1154 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the depreciation in the second year is } \$1154$$
criteria: Finds the value after one year, $\$4440$, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
The only deduction is the depreciation from part (a), $\$1154$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{taxable income} &= 110\,000-1154 \\ &= \$108\,846 \end{aligned}$$
This lies in the bracket $\$90\,001-\$180\,000$: $\$20\,797$ plus $37$c for each $\$1$ over $\$90\,000$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{tax} &= 20\,797+0.37\times(108\,846-90\,000) \\ &= 20\,797+0.37\times 18\,846 \\ &= 20\,797+6973.02 \\ &= \$27\,770.02 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{she pays } \$27\,770.02 \text{ in tax}$$
criteria: Finds the taxable income and selects the correct tax bracket, or equivalent merit
Finds the taxable income $\$108\,846$, or equivalent merit

meta.generated_note: The question does not say which year's depreciation applies; used the $1154 from part (a) as stated.

parts.latex:
Chris purchased a laptop for \$2 999.00 exactly 3 years ago.

He claims 15% depreciation per year using the declining balance method.

Calculate the current salvage value of the laptop.

solutions.latex:
For declining balance depreciation, $S = V_0(1-r)^n$, with $V_0 = 2999$, $r = 0.15$ and $n = 3$.
$$\begin{aligned} S &= 2999 \times (0.85)^3 \\ &= \$1841.76 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is option B.

parts.latex:
The car has an expected depreciation rate of $18\%$ per annum.

What is the salvage value of the car after 5 years?

solutions.latex:
Stamp duty is charged on the purchase price rounded up to the nearest $\$100$.

Purchase price $\$55\,950$ rounds up to $\$56\,000$.

$$\begin{aligned} \text{Stamp duty} &= 1300 + 6 \times 56\,000 \div 100 \\ &= 4660 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{stamp duty is } \$4660$$
criteria: Makes some progress with one error, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:

Using the declining balance formula $S=V_0(1-r)^n$:

\exfigure{2828_q4b_1}

figures.cap: graph of depreciating value of a laptop, passing through (3, 712)

parts.latex: Determine the annual percentage rate of depreciation, correct to two decimal places.
Work out the value of the laptop after 6 years.

solutions.latex:
From the graph, the value is $\$1500$ initially and $\$712$ after $3$ years.
$$1500(1 - r)^3 = 712$$
$$(1 - r)^3 = \dfrac{712}{1500}$$
$$1 - r = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{712}{1500}}$$
$$\begin{aligned} r &= 1 - \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{712}{1500}} \\ &= 0.2199 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ r = 21.99\%\ (\text{accept } 22\%)$$

meta.marker_note: Accept calculation with $22\%$ or correct follow through from part (a).

parts.latex: An asset depreciates to half its original value after 2 years using the declining balance method. What is the approximate annual rate of depreciation?

solutions.latex:
Using the declining balance formula, $S = V_0(1 - r)^n$:
$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{1}{2}V_0 &= V_0(1 - r)^2 \\ \dfrac{1}{2} &= (1 - r)^2 \\ \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2}} &= 1 - r \\ r &= 1 - \sqrt{\dfrac{1}{2}} \\ &= 0.293 \end{aligned}$$
The rate is $29.3\%$.
